non_blocking_suggestions: The seed is constructed by calling create_residual_from_appraisal and then immediately overriding kind and target_id via model_copy. This is correct and consistent with how the rest of the bridge layer stamps those fields, but a short inline comment noting 'kind and target_id are bridge-layer concerns not settable by create_residual_from_appraisal' would improve readability for future maintainers.

The bootstrap condition includes t4_signal.relational is not None. If a future T4 builder emits a non-None relational even on a neutral or positive day, the bootstrap would fire unexpectedly. Consider adding an explicit check that _t4_qualifying_event has a qualifying valence/type to make the guard self-documenting.
rationale: The Phase 26B bootstrap mechanism is correctly implemented: it creates the seed residual via create_residual_from_appraisal (settlement contract honored, aftershock_days=1, no direct ResidualEntry construction in bridge layer), stamps kind=relational and target_id via model_copy (legitimate bridge-layer concern), and inserts the seed before _t4_residuals_before is captured so _t4_residual_created remains False — preserving audit semantics. The seed fires only once (condition t4_residual is None ensures no repeat on subsequent days once a relational residual exists). The chain is bounded: aftershock_days=1 plus the existing wake-chain decay tests confirm no self-sustaining loop. The two modified test files (test_t4_p26b_exit.py, test_t2_t4_composition_audit.py) correctly update assertions from 0 to 1 relational residual to reflect the new bootstrap behavior, while preserving the intent that the wake-chain gate remains closed on the seed day. No forbidden files were modified (AppraisalSignal definition unchanged, T4 deterministic path unchanged, no new fields added to domain models).
